articleTitle: 24 GHz radar sensors for automotive applications
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Automotive radar systems using integrated 24 GHz radar sensor techniques are currently under development (see Klotz, M. and Rohling, H., 5th International Conference on Radar Systems, 1999). This paper describes a radar network consisting of four sensors distributed behind the front bumper of an experimental car. Each single sensor measures the target range with high accuracy. A multilateration technique is used in the radar network for precise azimuth angle estimation even in multiple-target situations. The system performance is shown in real traffic situations for parking aid, stop-and-go and blind spot applications.

articleTitle: Split post dielectric resonator technique for precise measurements of laminar dielectric specimens-measurement uncertainties
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A split-post dielectric resonator was used to measure solid laminar dielectric specimens which had been previously measured by a number of other techniques. Detailed error analysis of permittivity and dielectric loss tangent measurements has been performed. It was proved that, by using a 4 GHz split post resonator, it is possible to measure permittivity with uncertainties down to 0.3% and dielectric loss tangent with resolution 2/spl times/10/sup -5/ for well machined laminar specimens.

articleTitle: Maximum likelihood estimation of the number of looks in SAR images
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The number of effective looks in a SAR image is an essential parameter for determining the speckle level in the image. In particular, it permits the evaluation of the speckle standard normalized deviation in the image. This value is at the center of the majority of speckle filtering techniques. We propose to use a maximum likelihood approach based on a method of functional density estimation in order to estimate this parameter.

articleTitle: Microwave amplitude equalizer
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: This short paper presents the model of a broadband amplitude equalizer operating within the 6-18 GHz band. The equalizer attenuation decreases with increasing frequency, i.e., the equalizer characteristic behaves in opposition to any microwave passive components, e.g., cables, transmission lines, etc. Due to this, connecting the equalizer into a microwave system results in equalizing the frequency characteristics.

articleTitle: Multi-layer meander line polarizer for Ku band
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A multi-layered meander line polarizer for Ku band was analysed using the transmission matrix concept and empirical formulas for E and H mode susceptances. The influence of dielectric losses of substrates as well as glue layers have been studied numerically for a 4-section polarizer. The results of experimental verification of the design procedure are also presented with some conclusions concerning the influence of tolerances in meander line fabrication.

articleTitle: A 3D passive surveillance system VERA accuracy analysis
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The passive surveillance system VERA consists basically of three or more terrestrial stations receiving simultaneously the signal of an airborne secondary surveillance radar transponder. The emitter position is evaluated using the corresponding time of arrival (TOA) measurements. The system is produced in several versions, designed for various applications. The four position three-dimensional model of the VERA system is briefly described and the accuracy of aircraft position measurement is analysed and compared with experimental results. The effect of simultaneous direction of arrival (DOA) measurement is also evaluated and discussed.

articleTitle: Parameter study of a broadband uniplanar quasi-Yagi antenna
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A parameter study is performed of a broadband uniplanar quasi-Yagi antenna with regard to its design and use in a spatial power combiner. The uniplanar quasi-Yagi antenna consists of a director and a driver fed by a broadband microstrip to coplanar strip transition. The truncated ground plane on the backside of the substrate is used as a reflector. A 3D full-wave electromagnetic field analysis, using a commercially available 3D full-wave EM package, is applied to identify those parameters which most affect the design frequency and operational bandwidth of this antenna. Optimal design conditions are identified.

articleTitle: The simple method for analysis of nonlinear frequency distortions in FMCW radar
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The paper presents a simple method for the estimation of nonlinear frequency distortions of linear frequency modulated (LFM) signals used in FMCW radars. This method, derived from the polynomial model of a nonlinear LFM signal phase, is based on finding the maximum of the two-dimensional chirp-like transform of the IF signal obtained by mixing the transmitted LFM signal with its delayed copy. Using the suggested transform, we show the ability of the method to detect and classify signal distortions.

articleTitle: Phase noise in two-dimensional spectrum of video signal in FMCW homodyne radar
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Mapping of transmitted signal phase noise into amplitude spectra of a video signal in a frequency-modulated continuous wave homodyne radar with two-dimensional signal processing is studied for the example of an ideal stationary object and a free-running oscillator. Results of numerical simulations for a flicker FM noise-dominated source are given and discussed. Closed form analytical expressions for components of differential phase jitter are also given.

articleTitle: Microwave harmonic generation in fiber-optical links
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Optical transmission of microwave (MW) and millimeter-wave (MMW) signals have become an intensive research area in the last decade. There is a growing interest in optical processing of MW signals, phased array applications and wireless distribution of broadband data in fiber-fed MMW subscriber access systems. This paper extends the existing models of MW/MMW optical link that are based on optical intensity (see Frigyes, I. et al., Proc. of the 27th EuMC, 1997; Cox III, C.H. et al., MTT, vol.38, no.5, p.501-9, 1990). The model is suitable for estimating harmonic levels of the MW modulation signal generated in the optical path. Considering a MW fiber-optic link, both the optical transmitter and the receiver are responsible for harmonic generation. Furthermore the optical fiber itself inserted between the transmitter and receiver induces harmonics due to dispersion. Exact modelling of harmonic generation requires a calculation based on the optical field instead of purely on a intensity basis (see Hilt, A. et al., 1999; Maury, G. et al., 1999).

articleTitle: Doppler polarimetric ground clutter identification and suppression for atmospheric radars based on co-polar correlation
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: In this paper, a new clutter suppression technique is introduced. This clutter suppression method uses both Doppler and polarimetric information. Polarimetric properties of the target and clutter are calculated per Doppler frequency cell and, based on this information, clutter suppression is performed. This new clutter suppression technique is demonstrated with radar measurements of precipitation made by Delft Atmospheric Research Radar (DARR).

articleTitle: Broadband microwave phase detector with diode ring
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The broadband microwave phase detector with diode ring considered is useful both as a phase detector and frequency detector. The principle of operation of such a detector is presented, as well as output voltage characteristics for the theoretical model and real circuit.

articleTitle: Theory of high overtone bulk acoustic wave resonator as a gas sensor
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A one-dimensional model analysis based on the high overtone bulk acoustic wave resonator (HEAR) spectroscopy theory is developed for the description of the operation of gas sensors. The sensor model consists of a thin film transducer with film electrodes located on the face surface of the low acoustic loss material plate with the other surface of the plate covered with a gas sensitive layer. The model implies the fact that the thickness of this layer increases due to gas absorption resulting in the frequency change of the resonator. It was found analytically that the sensor sensitivity increases a hundred times when the initial thickness of the layer is close to a quarter of the acoustic wavelength.

articleTitle: Tunable dielectric resonator bandpass filter
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A simple but effective technique has been applied to magnetically tune the quasi-TE/sub 011/ mode dielectric resonator. The tuning was achieved by means of a ferrite rod situated centrally in the dielectric resonator and extending over the shield. The ferrite parameters were changed by DC magnetic field. The method assures the high quality factor of the resonator, over 3.4% tuning range and sufficiently good spurious response.

articleTitle: Photovaractor for optically controlled microwave circuits
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The photovaractor for optically controlled microwave circuits was designed and studied. The photovaractor module was fabricated as a planar p-i-n InP/InGaAs photodiode chip placed in a fibre optic matching receptacle. Study of C-V characteristics in the light illumination mode has shown that capacitance characteristics are strongly dependent on the light illumination power. These variations of the photovaractor diode capacitance are large enough to be used in optically controlled circuits such as oscillators, mixers and switchers.

articleTitle: Emulation of ad-hoc networks on IEEE 802.11
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: This paper reports on the emulation of ad-hoc networks based on the IEEE 802.11 standard using the Berkeley Network Simulator including its CMU Monarch (ad-hoc) extension (NS). We examined the emulation capabilities of the Network Simulator. Performance and verification tests also have been done using the emulator. Requirements of the emulator were tested. Some important attributes of emulation, like real-time requirements and CPU power were shown by the tests.

articleTitle: Applications of MEMS in communication satellites
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Micro-electro-mechanical-systems (MEMS) are finding more and more applications in microwave systems. Communications satellites, which typically have a large microwave hardware content, will be discussed as an example of these potential applications. In the first part, general MEMS technology and early examples will be described. Next, space applications of MEMS (sensors, actuators, propulsion etc.) in a communications satellite vehicle (bus) will be shown. Finally, microwave applications of MEMS in satellite payloads (switches, micromachined structures, tunable filters, and phased array antennas) will be presented.

articleTitle: Analysis of traffic distributions in GSM
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The main aim of this work is to study traffic models for mobile networks and to compare them with real data from a GSM operator. Accurate air interface traffic forecasting is of great importance in mobile networks for achieving quality and cost requirements. Previous studies of traffic modeling in mobile networks have tended to derive distributions to fit the measured data for the arrival rate and call holding processes or derive expressions for call blocking on the air interface for different handover and channel assignment procedures. In this work, call blocking and handover failure probabilities of the Telecel GSM network are presented. A theoretical analysis is compared with measured data from base station "Parede" in the south of Lisbon.

articleTitle: The 100W class A power amplifier for L-band T/R module
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A balanced high-power amplifier with class A silicon bipolar transistors for an L-band T/R module for active phased array radar is described. The amplifier was designed for maximum power and minimum transmittance distortion. The obtained parameters of the amplifier are as follow: output power at 1dB compression P/sub 1 dB/>49 dBm, linear gain |S21|>10 dB, and transmittance deviations during the RF pulse: phase /spl Delta/arg(S21)<0.9/spl deg/ and /spl Delta/P/sub out/< 0.2 dB.

articleTitle: Broadband helicon isolator for meter and decameter wave ranges
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The analysis of possible circuits for the realization of broadband isolators for meter and decameter wave ranges based on helicon resonators is carried out. The nodal model and matrix of scattering of an isolator is obtained. The possibility of extension of bandwidth up to an octave is shown.

articleTitle: Characterization of low loss dielectric materials in millimeter wave region using a whispering gallery mode resonator
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A new method for measuring the complex permittivity of a low loss material in the millimeter wave region is developed. The heart of the method is a higher order whispering gallery mode resonator which is made of the material under test. The method has a great advantage for millimeter measurements because the dielectric disk resonator does not need a shielding metal structure. Measured results of some plastic and ceramic materials in the 50 to 110 GHz band are presented.

articleTitle: A dedicated computer system for FM-CW radar applications
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: In this paper, a DSP based computer system for FM-CW radar applications is described. Besides data acquisition and storage, the computer system can be used for front-end data processing and system control. Processing includes filtering and clutter suppression. The radar for which the computer is designed is a multi parameter atmospheric profiler capable of doing Doppler and polarimetric measurements. The computer system allows for a measurement of the full polarimetric scattering matrix over 512 range cells and 512 Doppler cells in 2 sec. Radar system control includes the timing and the settings of the radar system together with linearity correction of the sweep oscillator.

articleTitle: RF material characterization using a large-diameter (76.8 mm) coaxial air line
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: We report on the development of a 76.84 mm (3.025 in) diameter coaxial air line system whose purpose is to measure the dielectric and magnetic properties of bulk dielectric and ferrite materials over a frequency range of approximately 0.3 - 1500 MHz. We summarize the relative advantages and disadvantages of using large-diameter coaxial air lines for material characterization and we discuss the particular problems associated with calibrating vector network analyzers in this form of transmission line. We also present broadband measurement data on two lossy materials, including a ferrite-loaded polymer and carbon-loaded concrete.

articleTitle: Using of sampling scope for antenna measurements in time and frequency domain
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The possibility of using a two-channel digital sampling oscilloscope for antenna pattern measurements in time domain and frequency domain is considered. The presence of the external trigger operating mode in the sampling scope enables it to be used for measurement in the frequency domain using the signal from the reference antenna for synchronisation. There is a possibility to use these methods for phased array adjustment.

articleTitle: One-dimensional analysis of microwave batch sterilization of water with continuous impedance matching
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A combined electromagnetic and thermal analysis of microwave batch sterilization of water is presented, based on a one-dimensional model, both with respect to the electromagnetic wave propagation and heat transfer. The model incorporates impedance matching tuners, which ape continuously optimized to maximize the power delivered to the water sample, whose parameters change with temperature. Numerical results are included showing typical power and transient temperature profiles in water.

articleTitle: New RF front end technologies
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: This paper provides an overview of numerous recent advancements in RF front end technology. Various techniques for designing novel front-end technology are outlined. Examples of the application of the active integrated antenna design approach are given for both the high-power transmitter and low-noise receiver modes. In addition, several architectures implementing novel mixer designs are presented to achieve baseband receivers and retrodirective arrays.

articleTitle: Complex layered arrays as photonic band-gap structures
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The reflective and transmitting properties of several layers of double-periodic arrays are studied. In the arrays, elements are conducting inclusions of various shapes. It is shown that in these structures all the phenomena recently found in dense wire grids with periodical defects (so called photonic band-gap structures) can be observed and explained in simple terms of interlayer and inclusion resonances. Frequency-selective (with two and more stop bands) and polarization transformation properties of these arrays are demonstrated.

articleTitle: The priority assignment for detected targets in multi-function radar
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: In a multi-function radar, there is a necessity to manage its very limited resources. This management should concern, among other things, the characterization of the importance of detected targets. Hence, information on those with lower priority will be refreshed more rarely. The ranking procedure is based on features recognized as important from the point of view of, for example, air force tactics and anti-aircraft defense. The presented paper describes a system that assigns ranks for all detected objects in real time and then puts targets in order of priority. The system is based on an artificial neuron structure. Methods of neuron learning are discussed.

articleTitle: Measurements of susceptibility due to paramagnetic impurities in sapphire using whispering gallery modes
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The microwave susceptibility due to paramagnetic impurities in monocrystalline sapphire has been evaluated based on measurements of the resonant frequency shifts of several whispering gallery modes (WGM) from the normal to the saturated spin state. Spin saturation was achieved by employing a microwave source at a frequency close to the frequency of electron spin resonance for the specific paramagnetic ions. The microwave susceptibility due to the presence of Cr/sup +3/ ions was measured and it proved to be highly anisotropic having the dominant component in the plane perpendicular to the anisotropy axis (C-axis) of sapphire crystal.

articleTitle: Radar signal detection algorithms using nonparametric estimates of noise distribution functions
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The new nonparametric algorithms of signal detection, based on Chentsov and Parzen estimates of a noise density function have been surveyed. The algorithms can be used for detection of signals on a set noise and reflections from an underlying surface, clouds, sea etc. The use of these estimates provides stability of the false alarm probability and high detection performance. The effectiveness of algorithms is researched by a Monte-Carlo method.

articleTitle: Multimode analysis of waveguide discontinuities using the concept of generalised scattering matrix and power waves
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The application of the power scattering matrix for the FDTD algorithm with impedance boundary conditions is presented. The power scattering matrix is obtained when the waveguide ports of the analysed structure are terminated by any convenient impedances. The conventional scattering matrix is then obtained by the appropriate matrix conversion.

articleTitle: Split post dielectric resonator technique for dielectric cure monitoring of structural adhesives
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The split post dielectric resonator (SPDR) technique has been used to monitor in situ changes in the dielectric constant and loss tangent in thermoset adhesives, as a result of the reduction of reactants of relatively low molecular weight. These dielectric studies appear to complement other polymer characterization techniques such as dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) and differential scanning calorimetric (DSC) methods. Although other types of dielectric cure monitoring devices are available, we feel that the split post dielectric resonator offers maximum sensitivity for determining the dielectric parameters directly and accurately.

articleTitle: The optimization of the transmittance phase changes of power amplifiers for T/R module of active phased array radar
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A method of limitation of the transmittance deviation during the RF pulse of power amplifiers for the T/R module of active phase array radar is described. The method is based on the load-pull technique and is examined using a GaAs MESFET transistor.

articleTitle: A microwave coherent polarimeter with velocity gating for road surface monitoring
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The presence of ice, water or snow on a road surface changes its microwave polarimetric scattering matrix. Safety in driving could be enhanced with a polarimeter able to warn the driver in real-time in case of dangerous situations. In this paper, a polarimeter realised with cheap components is presented.

articleTitle: Radar object recognition by wavelet transform and neural network
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: This paper presents a method of radar object recognition by wavelet transform and neural network. Analysing range profiles by wavelet transform can show information about the tracked object more clearly. It also gives a method of constructing a feature vector for automatic recognition so that the dimension of the feature vector may be much smaller than the dimension of the primitive echo signal. A three-layer backpropagation neural network is used as recognisor. This problem is aimed at radar systems with the duration of the transmitted pulses longer than the size of the object.

articleTitle: Power suppression mode in semiconductor synchronized microwave oscillators
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: An experimentally discovered and theoretically analyzed mode of power suppression of the output signal in a Gunn diode-based oscillator is described. It is established that the explored mode of the synchronized oscillator has an extremely high sensitivity to change in the natural frequency of the Gunn diode. The possibility is shown of using the power suppression mode in a semiconductor synchronized microwave oscillator as a method for high-precision indication of parameters changing for objects that are placed into the generator's resonator system.

articleTitle: A 4.4 GHz microwave thermometer with compensation of reflection coefficient
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The paper reviews the physical principles of thermal radiation measurement at microwave frequencies. A 4.4 GHz microwave thermometer with compensation of reflection coefficient and digital control loop is presented. The radiometer is applied to making three-dimensional thermal maps of human tissues. Reflection coefficient compensation is discussed, using as an example a simple model of noise power exchange at the antenna-object interface. In addition, measurements for various reflection coefficients (0.05+0.9) are presented in a graphical manner.

articleTitle: Resonance analysis of microwave cylindrical cavity using an electromagnetic simulator
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A new fast frequency sweep solution in Ansoft HFSS version 6 allowed us to obtain the frequency response of the imaginary part of the port's admittance and impedance of a closed cylindrical cavity. A comparison of analytical and simulated resonance frequencies and unloaded quality factors of the cavity modes proves that the microwave resonant structure parameters can be determined with a very high precision. A cylindrical TE/sub 011/-mode cavity, tightly coupled to the input and output ports, is then investigated. The comparison between simulated results and measured parameters of the cavity is also given.

articleTitle: 3-D electromagnetic analysis of the package influence on the IC performance
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: An integrated circuit package has been analyzed using the 3-dimensional FDTD simulator. The finite isolation between IC leads and the lead impedances can be precisely computed. The computed characteristics have been used to develop a circuit model of the package. Then the influence of the package on the integrated circuit performance has been investigated with high-frequency circuit simulators. Presented results show the necessity of including package properties in the RF and microwave IC design process.

articleTitle: Compensation of rain attenuation for Ka-band satellite systems
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The paper addresses the problem of compensation of attenuation due to rain for a satellite communication system operating in the Ka-band. The structure of a fade countermeasure (FCM) system is proposed and simulated with the use of recordings of signal level during real rain events. Key parameters of the FCM system are identified and their influence on the system performance is examined. Selected simulation results of the performance of a videoconferencing system with FCM system are presented.

articleTitle: Estimation of internal distribution of temperature inside biological tissues by means of multifrequency microwave thermograph
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The paper presents problems connected with thermal radiation of human bodies in the microwave range in respect of diagnosis of breast carcinoma. A mathematical model of transmission of thermal radiation through tissues is introduced and methods of measurement of temperature, depth and size of heat source, by means of multifrequency microwave thermography, are described. Theoretical considerations are supplemented with presentation of the results of experiments.

articleTitle: A method for evaluation of uncertainties of noise parameter measurement
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The assessment of uncertainties of two-port noise parameter measurement relies on modelling of sources of errors and an investigation of propagation of the errors through a measurement system. This approach is based on a simplified additive error model and small-change sensitivity analysis. The evaluated uncertainties agree with those observed in experiments. This method may be implemented in automatic noise measurement systems for online uncertainty assessment and for optimization of the design of an experiment.

articleTitle: Lowering the uncertainty in fast noise measurement procedures
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: To completely characterise the noise behaviour of a two port device, four noise parameters F/sub min/, R/sub n/, G/sub opt/ and B/sub opt/ must be determined. This paper reports improvements in the uncertainty related to the above parameters, taking into account measurement errors due both to the limited instrument precision and connection repeatability. Results are reported for noise characterisation of 0.3 /spl mu/m /spl delta/-doped HEMT devices by Alenia, demonstrating that the common hot-cold measurement procedure can result in an error confidence as low as 0.2% for all the noise parameters.

articleTitle: Gunn diode generator for frequency band 26-40 GHz
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: This paper presents the design principle of a Gunn diode generator with waveguide output, chip Gunn diode device and elements of an asymmetric strip line. Some of the dynamic characteristics showing the output power, frequency and the range of mechanical tuning within the frequency range 26-40 GHz are also presented.

articleTitle: A new approach to designing the transmission line band stop filters for antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A new algorithm for designing wideband band stop filters is presented. The filters under consideration are composed of noncommensurate transmission line sections whose characteristic impedances are limited by given permissible values. Due to that the filters designed in the proposed manner may be easily realizable, and the electrical strength of them may be taken into account during the design process.

articleTitle: Polarisation diversity in mobile communication
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The subject of this paper is the study of the polarisation properties and other parameters of antennas for use in a polarisation diversity application in the base station of a mobile communication system. The antenna main polarisation tilt angle is analysed for /spl plusmn/45 degrees or 0/90 degrees. The preferred orientation is proposed. Uplink and downlink aspects are analysed. It is concluded which kind of antenna is right for best diversity gain.

articleTitle: Structures of prototypes for broadband microwave filters, diplexers and matching networks
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: General structures and a classification of prototypes (for about 250 networks) for broadband microwave filters and matching networks for given complex load are presented. The peculiarities of synthesis methods, theoretical limitations and properties of input impedance for singly terminated and double terminated networks and frequency diplexers are described. Results of a computer simulation of frequency characteristics for different broadband filters and matching networks are presented.

articleTitle: Low order autoregressive (AR) models for FDTD analysis of microwave filters
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The forward-backward autoregressive model is applied to extract time signatures generated by the FDTD algorithm. It is shown that using simple techniques of model parameter selection one is able to reduce the model complexity for low and medium Q circuits.

articleTitle: The theory of power amplifiers with a polyharmonic operating
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: In this paper the main characteristics (such as drain efficiency and output power capability) of a power amplifier with polyharmonic operation are considered. The attempt is made to combine these characteristics for different polyharmonic operations (class E, class F, etc.) in a unified theory.

articleTitle: Technology and characterization of a fast MSM photodetector
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Metal-semiconductor-metal photodetectors (MSM PD) based on the InGaAs light-absorbing layer have been fabricated and characterized. It has been demonstrated that despite the non-optimized design, the devices operate well up to 3 Ghz and can compete with professional p-i-n diodes. The conclusions for future device improvement have been drawn.

articleTitle: Optical millimeter wave generation for cellular mobile systems
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: An optical millimeter wave generation approach is presented for cellular mobile systems. The well-known methods distribute the millimeter wave signal via fibers. They have drawbacks because they need very high speed photonic components which are expensive. That problem is overcome by the present approach utilizing an optically transmitted low-frequency reference signal to generate the millimeter wave carrier. This approach applies inexpensive photonic components and is less sensitive to the fiber dispersion.

articleTitle: Low-profile solutions for high-gain antennas and their measurements at millimeter wavelengths
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A low-profile antenna design for millimeter wave radio link applications is presented. The antenna has a simple planar array construction, high gain and low enough sidelobes to be ETSI compliant. Measurement with a hologram CATR (compact antenna test range) is also discussed and the results are compared with those from tests in a planar near-field scanning facility and from tests with the traditional far-field method.

articleTitle: CAD formulas and experiments for rectangular microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Calculations of several cases for rectangular microstrip patch antennas using a more accurate cavity model have been compared with the conventional cavity calculations, expressions generated by curve fitting to full wave solutions and moment method calculations for substrates with /spl epsiv//sub r/=10.8 and /spl epsiv//sub r/=6.45. Calculated as well as experimental values have been studied for different thickness and patch sizes.

articleTitle: Propagation in rectangular waveguides with a pseudochiral /spl Omega/ slab
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The transfer matrix approach is applied for analysis of waveguides loaded with a uniaxial pseudochiral /spl Omega/-slab. In particular a pseudochiral parallel plate and rectangular guides are investigated. Based on the numerical analysis the influence of the pseudochirality on propagation characteristics and field distribution are examined. Other features such as a field displacement phenomenon appearing in both the considered structures due to the pseudochirality are also discussed.

articleTitle: Generalized radar/radiometry imaging problems
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The results of spatio-temporal imaging simulation based on radar, synthetic aperture radar (SAR) and radiometry systems are presented. The analytical relationship between object scattering/emitting and the formed image is given and the general approach for the description of imaging system by means of Fredholm equation solution is developed. The potential limit of image resolution based on the Cramer-Rao inequality is estimated.

articleTitle: Algorithm of automatic choice of proper microwave oscillator parameters for oscillation conditions satisfying
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: This paper presents an algorithm to assist in automatic selection of proper values of geometrical and electrical parameters of an oscillator for oscillation condition satisfaction. The algorithm is described in order to assist and hasten the process of microwave oscillator design. The algorithm's general logical structure is described.

articleTitle: Whispering gallery modes in rutile resonators at millimeter wave frequencies
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Whispering gallery modes in single crystal rutile resonator were measured at the frequency range 15-30 GHz. Predicted and measured values of resonant frequencies for several WGM were in excellent agreement. Permittivity components parallel and perpendicular to anisotropy axis have been evaluated and their values were /spl epsi//sub /spl perp//=85.8/spl plusmn/0.2% and /spl epsi//sub /spl par//=163.2/spl plusmn/0.2% at room temperature and frequencies 15-30 GHz. Dielectric loss tangent components of rutile measured at room temperature and frequency of 25 GHz were tan/spl delta//sub /spl perp//=4.2/spl times/10/sup -4//spl plusmn/10% and tan/spl delta//sub /spl par//=5.7/spl times/10/sup -4//spl plusmn/10%.

articleTitle: Analysis of a coaxial line-circular waveguide junction used for measurement of materials
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A coaxial line terminated by a circular waveguide of arbitrary radius filled by a layered material medium is studied. A full-wave analysis of the structure via a mode-matching formulation is outlined. The equations are valid for both dielectric and magnetic materials. The model allows the study of the junction as a nondestructive testing tool. With an accurate theory, this scheme may be used to measure both complex permittivity and permeability of the material.

articleTitle: Radio wave propagation effects in high-altitude platform systems
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: In modern times an intensive development of different radiocommunication systems like cellular personal systems, has been noticed. The use of stratospheric high-altitude platforms as relay stations is being discussed by the ITU-R. This short paper presents the most important propagation effects in high-altitude platform links: the free-space loss, the atmospheric gas absorption, the attenuation due to clouds and the rain attenuation.

articleTitle: Antenna-coupled detector arrays in millimeter-wave indoor LAN
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The application of antenna-coupled detector arrays (rectennas) as receivers with the FM subcarrier frequency is demonstrated in MM wave "point-to-point" communication between computers particularly in the remote control system.

articleTitle: Measurements of high-speed MSM photodetectors
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: GaAs MSM photodetectors with AlAs/GaAs DBR structures designed for an operating wavelength of 840 nm were characterized in the frequency and time domains. The frequency response of the MSMs, using a lightwave set-up and HP8408 network analyzer, was measured. The photodetector response to the optical pulse of a fast laser diode excitation was evaluated. 3-dB bandwidth in excess of 4 GHz was obtained. Frequency and pulse responses dependence on photodetector bias was characterized.

articleTitle: New type of microstrip antenna with ferroelectric layer
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A new type of microstrip antenna is proposed using a voltage-controlled ferroelectric thin tape in the multilayered structure. This paper presents the ferroelectric thin tape, its theoretical analysis and design. The results indicate that this concept has many advantages, is very practical and promising. It has possibilities in several applications, e.g., in smart antennas.

articleTitle: Waveguide diplexer using E-plane tee of improved symmetry
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: It is proposed to use, in waveguide diplexers, an E-plane T-junction of improved symmetry for better performance. The characteristics of a waveguide diplexer with the conventional E-plane T-junction and the symmetrized one are compared.

articleTitle: Radio channel investigations for mobile systems
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A model and practical tool for radio channel investigations in outdoor and indoor areas are presented. This tool enables us to calculate and to analyze distribution of the electromagnetic field and to investigate the channel impulse and frequency responses. The basic purpose is to minimize interference effects of near and distant co-channel and neighbouring frequency transmitters.

articleTitle: Derivation of an equivalent circuit of Kurokawa-type oscillator resonance structure using an electromagnetic simulator
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A resonance structure of a cross-coupled coaxial-line-TM/sub 010/ mode cylindrical cavity together with a rectangular waveguide coupled with the cavity via a cavity-waveguide coupling slot and with a built-in band-reject filter (a choke and an absorber)-is analysed by means of an electromagnetic simulator. The analysis is separately carried out for two distinct parts of the structure: (a) a cross-coupled coaxial-line-cavity-waveguide three-port and (b) a choke-absorber one-port. Equivalent circuits, whose parameters are derived in an optimisation process, in which the circuit modelled S-parameters are fitted to those calculated by the electromagnetic solver, are proposed. As a result of such an analysis and optimisation, we obtain the frequency dependent characteristics of the whole two-port passive structure used in a single-cavity single Gunn-diode oscillator.

articleTitle: High efficiency HBV multipliers for millimeter wave generation
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: We describe the heterostructure barrier varactor (HBV) diode and its application in frequency multipliers. Different material systems and HBV models are described. In a frequency tripler experiment a maximum output power of 7.1 mW was generated at 221 GHz with a flange-to-flange efficiency of 7.9%.

articleTitle: Gain-bandwidth performance comparison of lumped and distributed element distributed amplifiers
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The gain-bandwidth performance (GBP) of a distributed amplifier (DA) comprising transmission lines (TL) is analyzed and compared to the GBP of a DA comprising lumped inductances. It is shown that the lumped element DA has the best performance. In addition to this, if the physical length of the TL is below a critical value, the GBP is almost constant, but above this critical value it degrades rapidly.

articleTitle: Beam shaping in radial line slot array antennas
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Beam shaping of a radial line slot array antenna is demonstrated using an approximate radiation model for this form of antenna. The procedure is demonstrated with the example of beam broadening of a Ku-band RLSA antenna having an assumed beam squint angle. Comparison between predicted and measured radiation patterns shows good agreement between theory and experiment.

articleTitle: Surface target tracking in WGS-84 coordinates
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The paper presents a method for surface target tracking using geographical WGS-84 coordinates instead of classical Cartesian coordinates. Use of geographical coordinates simplifies data generalization when more than one radar is used in command and control (CC) applications, and is very useful for airborne radars, when using the flat Cartesian coordinate system can introduce significant errors.

articleTitle: Automatic design of high frequency structures using a 3-D FD TD simulator in an optimisation loop
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A system for automatic design of microwave structures based on an electromagnetic FD-TD simulator working in an optimisation loop is presented. The paper describes the main elements of the system, which are: the FDTD simulator, the optimiser based on the Powell method, the parametric shape editor and the goal function calculator. Specific requirements imposed on each of the elements are discussed and the functioning of the entire system based on the QuickWave-3D Simulator by QWED is presented on practical examples.

articleTitle: Whispering gallery resonator method for permittivity measurements
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The new method of measuring permittivity is described. The measurements are performed using whispering gallery mode open dielectric resonators. The accuracy is assured by applications of the mode matching method. Three resonant modes (HE/sub 511/, HE/sub 611/ and HE/sub 711/) are used in the measurement procedure. The accuracy of the method is much better than 0.3% for the relative permittivity having values from 20 to 50.

articleTitle: "Microexpert"-the computer expert system for microwave oscillators design-final results
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: An expert system for designing microwave oscillators with multiple active devices and power combiners with a TM/sub 0n0/ mode cavity has been presented. The structure of the system combining the expert tools and ordinary optimization techniques that should be used during the design process of the microwave oscillators has been described. The system is based on real engineering data. It has a suite of programs for oscillator optimization as well as databases, a knowledge base and supervising program (inference engine). The whole inference engine has been elaborated from the background. By using this system both structural and parameter optimizations can be performed. For the oscillator structure chosen, the following optimization tasks can be performed: maximization of output power generated and minimization of frequency tuning characteristic ripple on a constrained set of parameters.

articleTitle: A wave approach to signal and noise modeling of dual-gate MESFET
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A new procedure for signal and noise modeling of dual-gate MESFET is described. The small-signal model is based on two cascaded single-gate MESFET intrinsic equivalent circuits embedded in a network representing device parasitics. Wave interpretation of noise is used for defining the noise parameters of each single gate MESFET. On the basis of that, a CAD-oriented procedure is developed for extracting dual-gate MESFET model parameters as well as noise wave temperatures. Modeled S and noise parameter characteristics are compared to measured ones and quite good agreement is observed.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave transceivers for point-to-point radios
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Millimeter-wave (MMW) point-to-point digital radios have been in production for several years. Due to the high demand of rapidly deployable cellular telephone networks, their market is growing worldwide. Point-to-multipoint systems have passed the R&D phase and are starting to reach the pre-production stage. This rapidly growing MMW wireless market is challenging the microwave industry with requirements for sophisticated MMW front-ends manufactured in high volumes but with prices significantly lower than similar products produced only a few years ago. This paper attempts to analyze the available market and the required technology today and in the near future.

articleTitle: Development of nanodispersible film material absorbing microwave radiation
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The results of theoretical and experimental examination of the electrodynamic performances of composite materials are given. A technique of calculation of electrodynamic parameters of materials with composite interior structure and examples of its practical usage are described. The results of an experimental investigation of the interaction of microwave radiation with thin layers of oxides of copper and iron are presented. X-ray and electron diffraction examination of film ferromagnetic materials after microwave action has shown, that their parameters are essentially distinct from the parameters of materials obtained with standard technologies at similar temperatures and energies. The obtained results indicate the possibility of using microwave radiation in chemical technological processes. An effect is described in which total absorption of electromagnetic energy takes place at the expense of a passing chemical reaction. This opens perspectives of making a new class of radioabsorption materials.

articleTitle: Materials for application in millimeter and submillimeter ranges
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Properties of different MM wave materials (liquid and solid dielectrics, semiconductors, ferrites, composite, building, natural and common use materials) at millimeter and submillimeter wavelengths are presented. These properties are of great interest for millimeter and submillimeter guiding and antenna systems including passive and active devices inserted in such systems, for millimeter and submillimeter propagation especially for indoor propagation, as well for introscopy problems and for materials and media content testing (first of all for aquametry). Here we present the results of our investigation at frequencies from 30 to 500 GHz of the complex refractive index for low loss and lossy dielectrics. For ferroelectrics, semiconductors, and ferrites, components of the ferrite permeability tensor were determined as well. For some kinds of artificial materials, e.g. clothing, effective refractive index, and transmission and reflection coefficients were measured.

articleTitle: Compact design of an S band low power correlation radar
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The construction of a correlation CW radar for the investigation of layered dielectric structures is presented. The means to decrease device dimensions and their impact on system performance is discussed. Compact design has been achieved through the application of SMD components and RF IC with a high degree of integration. Several device blocks are described in detail.

articleTitle: Resonant resistance of rectangular microstrip antenna-hybrid radiation mode approach
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The paper presents the application of the hybrid radiation (HR) modes of a microstrip line to the calculation of the resonant resistance of a rectangular microstrip patch antenna (RMPA). HR mode with phase constant /spl beta//spl ap/0 is chosen to approximate the EM field of the RMPA. Resonant resistances of example RMPA structures are calculated and compared with the results of rigorous analysis and experiment. Some conclusions concerning the usefulness of the approach are also presented.

articleTitle: Radiation efficiency of imperfect circular disk antennas
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: In this paper, we have proposed a full-wave approach to the analysis of the fundamental antenna effects in a circular-disk dielectric patch antenna on a thin substrate backed by a PEC ground plane and coaxially excited by a vertical electrical dipole. The method of analytical regularization combined with the Galerkin method has been used. Antenna characteristics, such as the surface and space-wave powers, directivity, radiation pattern, and radiation efficiency, have been obtained and analyzed for different values of the disk permittivity and frequency. The situation of surface-wave suppression in such antennas has been considered.

articleTitle: Space-based millimeter- and submillimeter-wave radiometric for impact monitoring
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The authors consider the design of a space system for detecting gas pollution of the atmosphere. The authors propose to use this system for checking observation of international agreements. The authors give the example of the equipment for checking the concentration of CO, CO/sub 2/, NO, SO/sub 2/, describe the construction and the block diagram of the multi-channel scanning radiometer and give the calculation of the error of measurement of harmful gas concentration in the atmosphere.

articleTitle: Dielectric resonators for low temperature electronics applications
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Single crystal materials exhibit much lower dielectric losses than their ceramic counterparts. The computed properties of high Q dielectric resonators which can be made of different single crystal materials are presented. Such resonators can operate at low temperatures with superconducting, metal or partly superconducting partly metal shield. For some single crystal cryogenic resonators Q-factors can be as high as 10/sup 10/ at 2 K and 10 GHz.

articleTitle: An introduction to the statistical theory of polarization parameters of fields scattered by complex radar objects
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The paper presents the main aspects of a new statistical theory based on a heuristic approach for the polarization properties of electromagnetic waves scattered by random complex radar objects (RCRO). The approach unites the methods of the statistical theory of random process outliers with the methods of statistical and physical optics.

articleTitle: Passive microwave complex of remote sensing for the detection of objects in the soil
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The paper deals with some grounding in theory of a passive radiometric complex designed to detect from a helicopter metal and non-metal objects in the soil at a depth of several metres. Experimental results obtained during tests of a complex prototype are presented as well. The complex can be applied in construction and repair works to detect underground utility systems. The complex is of particular interest for the detection of land mines which armed conflicts leave after their completion.

articleTitle: Multielement circuits for high frequency signals in receiving systems
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Receivers are main elements of communication, detecting and warning systems. They are used to detect and measure parameters of signals radiated by different sources of energy. They contain antenna arrays and signal forming circuits. The paper introduces a new design of signal forming circuit composed of quadrate couplers and phase shifters. The method and results of theoretical analysis as well as results of measurements in the range of 2-4 GHz are also presented.

articleTitle: Imaging of objects embedded in a lossy half-space with a stepped frequency synthetic aperture radar
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A stepped frequency continuous wave radar is used in a ground penetrating radar application for the high resolution imaging of surface laid or shallow buried objects. Effective sensing of low dielectric contrast objects (with respect to their host environment) is accomplished via integration methods to enhance the image processing gain. Specifically, a two-medium synthetic aperture treatment is applied and a frequency domain window implemented. These techniques taken in combination provide a significant improvement in radar detection performance and image contrast. To demonstrate the usefulness of these techniques, two field experiments using different antenna types were conducted and their results are reported.

articleTitle: Sub-millimeter switch radiometer with the pilot-signal
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Nowadays, there is the growing interest to exploration of the Earth's surface, the world oceans and the atmosphere by remote sensing using radiometry in the submillimeter range. This article considers the design of such radiometric superheterodyne receivers and the calculation of their potential sensitivity.

articleTitle: Geometrical representation of a monochromatic electromagnetic wave using the tangential vector approach
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Pulse radar has a very narrow band, so, to describe the state of the signal, it is possible to consider a single pulse as a monochromatic electromagnetic wave, which is completely polarized. A very useful representation of the electrical field is its spinor form which contains the complete information, even the zero phase. The aim of this work is to develop a coherent polarimetric model and to find a geometrical description of a monochromatic wave. The spinor form of the electrical field, its links to the coherency matrix and the Poincare sphere are introduced with the aim of obtaining a geometrical representation of the spinor. It consists, from the 'polarization point of view', of the polarization vector and a tangential plane to the Poincare sphere where it is possible to visualize the zero phase.

articleTitle: Modelling of wire lossy termination by using 3-D TLM method
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The resistive load at the end of a wire conductor is modelled by using the transmission-line modelling (TLM) method. For the wire modelling purpose, a wire node, as an integrated 3D TLM solution, is implemented in the developed software. Two models, for describing lossy termination of wire conductor and its connection to another structures, are proposed and verified by the appropriate examples. Calculated results are presented in the frequency domain and compared with the results obtained by using miniNEC and NEC2 simulators.

articleTitle: Microwave holography
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: High-quality measurements can be made of antenna surface (aperture illumination) using microwave holographic metrology, a specialized from of bistatic CW inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging that can be readily implemented on both near- and far-field ranges. In most ranges no additional hardware is required, as the microwave holographic technique is compatible with all types of antennas. In reflector antennas it can provide detailed maps of reflector surface currents, aperture illumination and surface shape errors. In phased-array antennas, holography can provide maps of aperture illumination, element weights, and geometric errors. This technique can also be successfully involved in evaluating the performance of antenna far-field test ranges by producing microwave images showing the distribution and level of scattering artifacts.

articleTitle: Characterization of vector network analyzer coaxial calibration components
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Resonance measurements have been applied in a procedure of low-loss coaxial standard components characterization. The paper outlines a method which gives not only the electrical length of the component in question but also provides data permitting us to develop the component's equivalent circuit. Characterization results of components from 2.92 mm calibration kit have been given. The distinct advantages of the developed approach are its high accuracy and the lack of stringent requirements on the employed network analyzer calibration accuracy.

articleTitle: A planar receive mode active phased array
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A 16-element planar active phased array in L-band, in its receive mode of operation, has been presented, for an experimental study on its radiation pattern characteristics in realising low-sidelobe performance and beam steering over the array scan angle. The results on this small-size active phased array, with a hardware simulator, have provided solutions to problems due to phase and amplitude quantisation, mutual coupling between the radiating elements, and the correction of phase and amplitude errors in the array excitation coefficients over a large frequency band of operation and over a wide array scan angle.

articleTitle: System for automatic measurements of intermodulation distortion in CATV networks
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Some disadvantageous effects caused by intermodulation distortion (IMD) in cable television networks are described. A system for automatic measurement of unwanted intermodulation products in CATV equipment is presented. Three different methods of measurement included in the system are mentioned. The system is suitable for different kinds of measurements and can be used for homologation tests of equipment.

articleTitle: Switched pulsed multiport for transmittance measurements
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The concept of a network for the measuring system of a scattering matrix of two-ports is presented. The network contains only two power meters instead of eight as in the classic dual six-port technique. The proposed design is not only more economical (fewer power meters) but also more accurate due to long-term instability of sensitivity. The main advantage of this circuit is the possibility of microwave pulse excitation. This circuit could be applied for measurement of power transistors in pulsed mode.

articleTitle: International Research Centre for Telecommunications-transmission and Radar (IRCTR)
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The Faculty of Information Technology and Systems (ITS) of Delft University of Technology (DUT) has developed an efficient and effective strategy for the implementation of research programs in the fields of telecommunications transmission and radar, the International Research Centre for Telecommunications transmission and Radar (IRCTR). Under the auspices of the IRCTR, cooperation with a large number of national and internally scientific institutes and companies has been established. For the last decade many companies, institutions and universities have participated in the radar and remote sensing research activities of DUT. As a result of that, the radar technology and systems, antennas and propagation and remote sensing research carried out at the Delft University of Technology has gained national and international recognition. In addition to radar there are the immense developments taking place in wireless communications which need to be addressed. Broadband communications are growing sectors with important applications in office automation, logistics services, personal communications and satellite communications. Unique research facilities for radars and communications have been built. These include DARR (Delft Atmospheric Research Radar), SOLIDAR (solid state radar), TARA (transportable atmospheric radar), DUCAT (Delft University Chamber for Antenna Tests) and CM-MM wave test and measurement equipment, as well as unique real-time computer and signal processing systems.

articleTitle: Radar processing of 2/sup n/-1 and 2/sup n/ PRN coded waveforms
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The processing of waveforms that are not LFM requires that the bandwidth of the signal be considered. Pseudo-random noise coded waveforms are now being used by cellular telephones and are being considered for use in radar systems. With the prevalence of digital signal processing (DSP) hardware, it is appears that the radar community has accepted that DSP equipment can process these waveforms. They can, but the use of the fast Fourier transform (FFT) doubles the range sidelobes. This paper discusses how processing these waveforms can alter their capabilities.

articleTitle: The antenna system of Mars-rover
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The paper describes two variants of antenna system construction for a Mars-rover intended for application in the structure of an onboard radio complex. It provides for receiving commands and transmitting information in C-frequency band. The first variant uses a parabolic reflector antenna with an electromechanical drive which ensures program guidance in extreme conditions. In the second variant, there is applied a slotted waveguide array with electronic control on the elevation coordinate.

articleTitle: Faster analysis of microwave engineering problems with multithread FDTD multiprocessor PCs
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Two multithread FDTD algorithms have been developed, and their applicability to faster analysis of microwave engineering problems has been demonstrated. MS-FDTD is based on low-order spatial decomposition and subcircuit calculations on separate processors. MF-FDTD performs parallel updating of the three orthogonal field components. The algorithms have been tested on 2- and 4-processor PC, where speed-up factors of 1.5 and 2.1 have been obtained for MF-FDTD and 1.5-1.7 for MS-FDTD respectively.

articleTitle: The theory of high quality electromagnetic oscillations in the multilayer spherical resonator
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The paper investigates the selection of the electromagnetic modes of a dielectric sphere in a compound multilayer resonator of optical frequencies. The waveguide properties of the spherical stack are investigated for systems of optical layers with arbitrary ratio between layer thickness and wavelength. The appropriate matrix formalism is developed. Both the reflection coefficient and the impedance of the stack are calculated. Depending on the number of layers, it is possible to decrease sharply the impedance of the system. It is shown that increasing the number of layers in the stack considerably increases the quality of oscillations. We offer to use such systems in optical communication systems for processing of signals.

articleTitle: Glass technology for MMIC
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A new approach to the design of microwave monolithic integrated circuits (MMIC) is presented in this paper. The technology uses thick glass layers on the silicon in order to reduce parasitic capacitance introduced by metallic layers deposited on the dielectric layer of the MMIC. It was applied to construct a microwave monolithic switch with a single input and three outputs.

articleTitle: Optically-controlled microwave PSK modulator
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: In our transmission system there was a need to use a binary PSK modulator. However there was a condition assuming a microwave signal phase control by means of an optical fibre link. To accomplish these requirements optically controlled microwave phase shifters and a 3 dB-quadrature (90/spl deg/) microwave coupler were used. The simulations and the measurements of the optically controlled PSK modulator were investigated and presented.

articleTitle: Distortion and noise problems of subcarrier multiplexed optical systems
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Investigation of subcarrier multiplexed optical subsystems for optically supported communication systems is presented. Noise and spurious free dynamic range are the main parameters, which is determined by the applied optical transmission. The frequency dependence of these parameters and optimal frequency chosen is presented.

articleTitle: Selected problems of 3-D target tracking
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The paper presents selected problems of tracking targets in 3D space, when the only source of measurement data is a primary radar. A radar measures target position in polar coordinates giving three independent readouts - target range to the radar, line of sight azimuth from the north and line of sight elevation (from the Earth surface). Target motion equations for the radar polar coordinates are nonlinear. Most trackers work in their natural Cartesian coordinate system, where motion equations are linear and measurement equations are nonlinear. The necessity for equation linearization, required in Kalman filtering introduces significant errors when measurement nonlinearities are present. These nonlinearities are discussed and modifications of the Kalman filter are proposed to deal with these nonlinearities.

articleTitle: PHEMT transistor models for accurate CAD of MMIC amplifiers
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Selected models of PHEMT transistors are presented for the popular Philips D02AH process. The models are based on a set of measurements of transistor parameters and have been verified against measurements of fabricated MMIC amplifiers. The usefulness of particular models for the CAD of microwave circuits is discussed.

articleTitle: Space discretising time domain methods for the numerical modelling of electromagnetic coupling in EMC
