publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: An overview is given on numerical methods for the efficient modelling of electromagnetic coupling phenomena involving the space discretising transmission line matrix (TLM) method. We consider objects which may have a complex structure of dielectric, lossy and conducting material which are separated by regions of homogenous material. The highly efficient method of adapted radiating boundaries (ARB) and the hybrid TLM-integral equation method are described combining the space discretising TLM method with a Green's function approach. The computational effort of the hybrid methods, the TLM method and the FDTD method is compared.

articleTitle: Researching of selected anti-clutter and anti-interference algorithms using recorded radar signals
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Examinations of selected anti-clutter and anti-interference algorithms in the MTD system are described in the paper. Low PRF surveillance radar with a pencil beam is considered. The research was performed using real radar signals and the results prove the high usefulness of the algorithms in real conditions.

articleTitle: Microwave properties of InGaAlAs resonant-tunneling optical modulators
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Impedance of resonant-tunneling heterostructure diodes (RTD) based on InGaAlAs and designed for modulation of optical radiation was experimentally studied in the frequency range of 45 MHz-18 GHz. The dependence of the equivalent circuit parameters versus bias voltage was analyzed and the current harmonic spectrum at varistor frequency multiplication was calculated. The effect of frequency multiplication was experimentally demonstrated at low frequencies.

articleTitle: Research of STC influence on radar signal compression quality
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Research results concerning the influence of a high-frequency attenuator realising the STC process on a output signal are described. Especially the relation between the attenuator's amplitude-phase characteristic and signal shape at a matched filter output is considered. The paper concerns radar wide spectrum signals as follows: LFM signal, biphase coded signal and polyphase coded signal. Such signal characteristics as PSL and a mainlobe width after compression are used for comparative analysis.

articleTitle: Degradation of the 2-D complex source point beam due to a circular dielectric radome
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The influence of the dielectric circular cylindrical radome on the antenna parameters such as directivity, gain, total radiated and absorbed power and pointing error are studied for both E- and H-polarizations. The beam field is simulated by the complex source point (CSP) beams radiating from inside of a homogeneous layered dielectric cylinder taken as a model of the radome. Such physical effects as directivity degradation or improvement due to a dielectric shell and a non-zero beam pointing error have been studied in an accurate manner.

articleTitle: Module antenna on multilayer dielectric
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Module antennas, consisting of 8 or 16 radiating elements, realized in stripline technology for the 1.8 GHz frequency band are presented in this paper. A practical realization of the radiating elements and the results of measurements are also presented here as a possibility of the practical application of these modules in planar array antennas.

articleTitle: Error of measurement of radio-brightness temperature of the underlying surface during space monitoring of the Earth
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The authors consider the main components of the error of measurement of the radio-brightness temperature of the Earth, including the background radiation of the Sun, and give an example of calculation for different reception frequencies.

articleTitle: 3D map features extraction from radar and visible remotely sensed image fusion
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: This paper presents an overview of a satellite image fusion system for mapping applications. The map features to extract include roads, railroads, energy transmission lines and some types of rivers. Actually, the only data source used for their extraction is aerial black and white photographs. The objective here is to fuse multi-source and multi-type information in a semi-automatic intelligent system. The used information ranges from satellite images (visible and radar) to domain-based models and expert modeled knowledge, strategies and rules.

articleTitle: Bistatic polarization properties of complex radar objects from monostatic measurements
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The paper concentrates on deriving the bistatic polarimetric RCS from monostatic measurements. The simplest representation of a complex object is used in the analysis. Both numerical and experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Complex permittivity measurements of single-crystal and ceramic strontium titanate at microwave frequencies and cryogenic temperatures
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The permittivity and dielectric loss tangent of bulk strontium titanate were measured from 4 to 300 K, at frequencies from 400 MHz to 3.8 GHz, using a dielectric rod-resonator technique. Single-crystal and ceramic SrTiO/sub 3/ samples were both investigated. Significant differences in permittivity and losses were observed between single-crystal and ceramic materials at cryogenic temperatures. When measured at liquid nitrogen temperatures, the single-crystal sample dielectric loss tangent was approximately 10/sup -4/.

articleTitle: Statistical verification of relation between L.F. and H.F. noise level of bipolar transistors
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: In this paper, statistical investigations of the relationship between L.F. noise and H.F. noise of type BF200 bipolar transistors are described. 1/f noise is the main kind of low frequency noise in semiconductors and semiconductor devices. The results of comparative measurements of the low frequency noise in selected bipolar transistors, designated to work in different frequency ranges, are also presented.

articleTitle: Recent advances in radar technology in Telecommunications Research Institute
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: This paper presents a view of the connection between progress in radar and microwave technology and shows some new products of the Telecommunications Research Institute of Poland. These products include reconnaissance equipment and command control systems for the Polish armed forces and for export.

articleTitle: Fast and accurate analysis of whispering gallery modes by the finite difference frequency domain method
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The analysis of whispering gallery modes in a cylindrical sapphire resonator is shown. The formulation involves only two components of the electric flux density. Using the FDFD method on Yee's mesh, the electromagnetic problem is converted to a standard nonsymmetric matrix eigenvalue problem with a highly sparse and structured matrix. The resonant modes are found by means of the implicitly restarted Arnoldi method with Chebyshev acceleration. Is is shown that the application of Chebyshev preconditioning allows one to significantly reduce the computing time without increasing the memory cost.

articleTitle: Numerical modeling the directivity properties of antennas
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The technique consisting of the statement and the solution of the appropriate synthesis problems for investigation of the directivity properties of antennas is described. The amplitude radiation pattern is considered as the directivity characteristic of the antenna. The synthesis problem is formulated in the variational statement and consists in optimization of functional, which characterizes the proximity of the obtained (synthesized) and required (prescribed) amplitude radiation patterns. This optimization can be carried out by two methods. The algorithms are proposed and the examples of computer-aided modeling of the radiation pattern of a cylindrical array are presented.

articleTitle: Constant co-polarized echo curves on the Poincare sphere
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A set of useful formulae has been presented allowing for computation of the equipower curves on the Poincare sphere of the co-polarized radar returns for both monostatic and bistatic scattering.

articleTitle: Noise figure measurement uncertainty caused by low gain of the two-port under test
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The methods for direct-reading noise figure measurements of a low-gain two-port under test (TUT) are briefly described. Measurement error caused by the component dependent on the low gain of the TUT is discussed for the conventional noise figure measurement method, and for methods with elimination of the influence on indicator readings of the receiver noise figure as well as of both the receiver noise figure and the TUT gain. Generalized suppression for the measurement error caused by a low gain of the TUT, while different methods are used, is presented in the paper. The TUT's gain measurement by means of automatic noise figure meters is presented. A problem exists in such a measurement for the purpose of automatic correction of the noise figure measurement results, because only an insertion gain instead of an available gain can be measured.

articleTitle: The method and results of the analysis of a circular antenna array composed of helical antennas
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A universal software complex is described. The complex allows us to calculate the electrodynamic characteristics of scattering and radiation of objects that have complicated geometry and allows net-wire approximation. The analysis is based on the numerical solution of integral equations for current in a thin conductor. By a similar method a circular antenna array consisting of helical antennas was investigated. The dependence of electrodynamic characteristics of the antenna array on geometric parameters of radiators, their quantity and location, is ascertained.

articleTitle: Microwave Schottky diode with beam-lead contacts
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: This paper presents a prototype Schottky diode with beam-lead contacts. The prototype was elaborated in the Microwave Department at the Institute of Electron Technology in Warsaw. The results of measurements for the prototype diodes are included.

articleTitle: Improvement of identification of weak-contrast radiolocation targets during monitoring of the Earth surface by radiopolarimetry
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: This article deals with the aspects of application of polarization processing to improve identification of weak-contrast Earth covers. The closest attention is paid to the analysis of the influence of polarization characteristics of objects including phase and correlation properties of scattering matrix elements on their identification. The authors calculated values of the optimal polarization basis and contrast gain as compared with the initial for several Earth covers for the diagonal and cross elements of the scattering matrix.

articleTitle: Theoretical and experimental approaches to analysis of irregular dispersion of electrodynamic structures
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The dispersion laws (spectral characteristics) considering the Morse critical points (MCP) are developed from the rigorous solution of homogeneous boundary value problem of a laterally inhomogeneous dielectric layer. The knowledge of the anomalies of the spectra near the MCP, feasibility of their analytical treatment by the both direct numerical analytical method and an alternative approach based on experimental results, and dispersion equations of the free oscillations provide the basis on which the local equations of the space-time evolution of the layer field are furnished near the MCP of irregular dispersion.

articleTitle: Interaction of an electrostatic field with a dielectric body
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The results of designing an integro-differential model of a dielectric cylinder with a fractal surface are presented. The integro-differential characteristic of component of an electrostatic field near to a rough surface are obtained. The figure of the deformation of a homogeneous field by the dielectric cylinder is shown. The numerical calculation results of a field structure are presented.

articleTitle: Acousto-optic phase processor of high frequency signals
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The system for an acousto-optic processor for phase and phase difference measurements (AOPP) of high frequency signals is considered in the paper. Interaction between the laser beam and acoustic waves results in the appearance of an interference pattern in the focal plane of an analysing lens. All parts of the AOPP system are discussed in detail. The analysis of the influence of disturbing factors on the interference pattern is also discussed.

articleTitle: Thick-films beyond the 1 GHz barrier
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Thick-film technology has shown significant progress in interconnection density using photopatterning technology, lower dielectric constant and lower loss dielectrics, higher conductivity conductors and buried resistors and capacitors integral with the substrate. These advances coupled with thermal and reliability advantages of thick-films have created a new generation of thick-film technology suitable for many microwave designs. The paper reviews new thick-film materials and processes developed to extend the capability of conventional MCM-C technology in microwave applications.

articleTitle: Design of suspended substrate stripline band-pass filter with optimal redundancy parameter
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A design method for narrowband suspended substrate stripline band-pass filters is presented. A generalized Chebyshev or Cauer low-pass prototype filter can be used, providing a suitable form of realization in suspended substrate technology. This design method is based on using Norton's equivalencies and calculating value of optimal redundancy parameter to get a network with a minimum spread of element values. Results from the designed device show that the method of realizing such a filter is viable for many applications.

articleTitle: Research of metallic and dielectric underground objects on the basis of original computer recognition technique of reflected radio signals
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: An original recognition technique based on collative classifiers is proposed, enabling the detection and identification of buried objects. This method was previously used for the automatic verification of subscripts. The sequence of classifiers was designed, each of which enables a decision to be made concerning the presence of a given feature in the measured object. The use of different integral features for recognition was investigated. Some experiments were made which showed the possibility of using the proposed method to solve practical problems of object identification.

articleTitle: Optical-microwave transmission system with subcarrier multiplexing for industrial measurement systems
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: We describe a short-distance three-channel optical-microwave link with subcarrier multiplexing for transmission of digital and/or analog data between different points of industrial measurement systems. The optical fiber link operates with a Fabry-Perot laser at 1300 nm, multimode fiber and PIN photodiode receiver. From a microwave point of view three carriers with frequencies 600 MHz, 800 MHz and 1000 MHz were chosen. The structure and main parameters of the link are reported and discussed.

articleTitle: Analysis of the world ocean parameters with the help of radiometric satellite system "Delta-2D"
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A brief description of the scanning radiometer "Delta-2D" installed in the satellite "Ocean-O" and analysis of the first results of the processing of the obtained information are presented. The basic aspects of the application of the radiometric complex for solving the problem of global monitoring of the water surface are considered.

articleTitle: Characteristic impedance of a TEM transmission line with non standard inner conductor
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The characteristic impedance of a TEM air-dielectric transmission line has been found for non-standard inner conductor situated inside an outer rectangular conductor or between two parallel plane outer conductors. Examples of diagrams of electric field distributions for cross-sections of the line for different parameters of the inner conductor and a graph of the characteristic impedance of the line versus these parameters are given. They are obtained using numerical techniques to solve the boundary value problem for this line. The line has good properties in comparison to other TEM type transmission lines.

articleTitle: Optimal receiver for touch signal detection
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The first part of this paper represents by means of the functional block diagram the optical infrared touch interface whose function is detection of touch on the screen of the touch terminal/monitor. Then an optimal receiver is formed for separation of the active component of the touch signal for the case when white Gaussian noise is superimposed. In the second part of this paper the error probability in making a decision on the existence or non-existence of the optical infrared beam between the transmitter and the receiver of the selected optical infrared pair is calculated. On the basis of this the optimal decision threshold is determined.

articleTitle: Wideband dispersive delay lines with two nonperiodic dispersive transducers
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A dispersive delay line with two nonperiodic dispersive transducers was described. This construction can be used to design wideband DDL with relatively low insertion loss. A DDL with centre frequency 70 MHz and bandwidth 40 MHz was designed and manufactured. The slanted transducer technique used to eliminate interelectrode reflections and Fresnel ripple was also presented.

articleTitle: Side scan sonar and interferometric noise
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: This paper concerns the description of different noise sources encountered as well as the impact of each of these sources through sonar interferometric data acquisition. The impact of noise is directly linked to the ability of the Vernier device to determine the 2/spl pi/ ambiguity of the phase measure and to know the altitude of the bottom. The main conclusion of this paper concerns the theoretical interest of the conducted approach in terms of the obtained results as well as in order to reduce the impact of these noise sources through the physical and the analytical comprehension of the data acquisition process.

articleTitle: Characteristics of the indoor propagation channel in 1.9 GHz band
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: This paper presents results of propagation measurements using a network analyser carried out in the frequency range 1.8-2.0 GHz inside a building. Wideband properties of the channel, described through mean delay and delay spread, and narrowband local statistics of the received power have been presented. For each transmitter and receiver antenna location, two propagation cases have been considered, line of sight (LOS) and obstructed line of sight (NLOS)-the direct path component was attenuated by a radio absorbing mat near the receiver. From our measurements, there is a clear indication that, in microcellular systems, the direct ray propagation situation should be preferred.

articleTitle: Synthesis and analysis of the long range radar transmitting antenna feeding network
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Discussion of the shaped beam pattern synthesis methods of a long-range radar antenna is presented. The optimised excitement current distribution of the transmitting array antenna is assumed as a base of the antenna feeding network design. Analysis of the hybrid waveguide-TEM line feeding network includes influence of the power dissipation and frequency change in the operational band. Monte-Carlo statistical analysis is used to predict the sensitivity of the antenna pattern parameters.

articleTitle: Coupled mode model of distributed ferrite microstrip line circulators
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A coupled mode approach has been applied to investigate the axially magnetized ferrite coupled (FCL) microstrip junction. The scattering properties of the junction are obtained and applications of FCL in microstrip distributed circulators are discussed. The performance of a microstrip FCL circulator is investigated by numerical experiment and good agreement with previously published results is obtained.

articleTitle: Radar measuring of turbulence intensity in clouds and precipitation
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: This work resolves the task of synthesising a complex algorithm for turbulence detection in weather objects and the measurement of turbulence intensity. The task of radar detection and measurement of turbulence in clouds has been urgent for several decades. Two main groups of informative parameters of echo-signal are known: amplitude (connected with reflectivity) and spectral (connected with Doppler spectrum). They display the characteristics of turbulence in two different ways. Their applications give various results not only in quantitative but also in qualitative terms. The valuation of spectral parameters permits the site of the turbulent zone to be rather precisely attached to the coordinates of the scattering volume. The application of amplitude parameters gives only the integrated valuation of turbulence danger in a rather extensive zone of cloud as a whole. Nevertheless, the idea of using the parameters of both groups remains a fruitful one. The given work shows some new opportunities for the localization of turbulent zones with the help of conventional airborne weather radar.

articleTitle: Dispersive filter having long impulse response
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: This paper consists of the theoretical results of surface acoustic wave dispersive delay lines (DDL) with large time-bandwidth (BT) product utilising long impulse response T of DDL. The long time duration in cascaded connection of the same single DDL has been achieved. Results of the calculations for chosen value BT=216 are presented. This paper contains the computer simulation of the pulse compression as well.

articleTitle: Polarisation of electromagnetic waves in four-dimensional Euclidean space
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Polarisation analysis of an electromagnetic wave is accomplished in a four-dimensional Euclidean space of the wave's amplitudes. Evolution of the amplitudes is represented by the motion over the surface of a three-dimensional S/sup /spl delta// sphere. It is shown that the commonly used three-dimensional space of the Stokes parameters, as well as the corresponding S/sup /spl delta// Poincare sphere, are particular mappings of the four-dimensional space onto the three-dimensional one. Some properties of electromagnetic wave evolution in four-dimensional space are discussed.

articleTitle: Computer aided design of a high performance slotted waveguide array antenna for maritime patrol radar applications
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The present paper deals with the design and development of an horizontally polarised, lightweight, high-performance slotted waveguide array antenna in X-band for maritime patrol radar applications. A design methodology making use of extensive electromagnetic modelling where all the radiating and coupling slots are characterised using the method of moments and feed networks using FEM have been used. The construction method uses a standard bonding technique and fixing systems to lower costs and realise mass production instead of the complicated dipbrazing process.

articleTitle: Pulse-excited six-port reflectometer
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A multi-port reflectometer which allows us to determine a complex reflectance in pulse mode of the device under test is proposed. The reflectometer is based on a symmetrical five-port junction, directional coupler and diode detectors. The hardware configuration of the six-port junction and its calibration as well as the linearization of the diode detectors have been investigated. The experimental results for several terminations measured by the proposed reflectometer working under pulse excitation are compared with data measured by a Hewlett-Packard network analyzer at the selected frequencies.

articleTitle: New method of phase noise and intermodulation distortion reduction in high-order QAM systems
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Modern digital communication systems, such as microwave and millimeter wave point-to-point radios and local multipoint distribution system (LMDS) equipment now employ high-order quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM). In addition to the well known effect of additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) on a QAM system's performance, phase noise and 3rd order intermodulation distortion (IMD) can also be major contributors to system performance degradation. This paper presents a simple analog distortion cancellation method which consists of a low-frequency feedback circuit connected between the FET output (drain) and the input (gate). This low-frequency feedback integrated with active bias is used to reduce phase noise and 3rd order IMD product by approximately 7 dB.

articleTitle: Measurement of surface profiles of a slag temperature by the remote radiometric method
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Theoretical fundamentals and results of measuring the temperature profiles inside a slag layer above molten metal by a new remote method have been considered. The influence of different methods of antenna array focusing on measurement accuracy have been analyzed. The universality of the proposed method makes possible its effective application to solve any problems where the reconstruction of near-surface profiles is necessary.

articleTitle: Antennas of vehicles landing on a planet surface
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The antenna systems designed under the international projects "Mars-96" and "Phobos" are described. In flight, the antenna system of a small station landing on Mars is packed under protective petals of the station and is opened on the surface with the help of flexible legs. The original scheme of excitation in the form of compact strip-geometry is described. The antenna system of the mobile vehicle landing on Phobos provides an omnidirectional pattern on the basis of the combination of antenna methods with methods of processing the received signal. The high efficiency of the antenna results from its construction in the form of an active antenna.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave imaging systems
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The state-of-the-art in development of millimeter wave imaging systems based on far-field and near-field remote testing is analyzed and discussed. It is definitely shown that MMW techniques give new practical opportunities in comparison with similar microwave or infrared systems and new types of semiconductor devices, waveguides and antennas impose the future progress in this area.

articleTitle: MOVPE InP based material for millimeter and submillimeter wave generation and amplification
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The potential of the MOVPE growth process for millimeter and submillimeter wave generation and amplification is presented. The increase in layer quality, the improved homogeneity and purity, the precision of mono-layers growth and wide spectrum III-V compounds makes MOVPE techniques very attractive for modern device applications. The characterisation results of the heterostructures dedicated for HBVs (heterostructure barrier varactors) and 2-DEG transistors (HEMT) are described.

articleTitle: Stability and nonlinear dynamics of directly modulated high-speed long-wavelength laser diodes
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Investigation and modeling of the effect of recombination and gain nonlinearities caused both by saturation and nonlinear dependence on carrier concentration on modulation response of high-speed long-wavelength bulk semiconductor lasers under moderate and strong modulation are presented. It is shown that increase in the injection current modulation depth leads to the fast distortion of harmonic response which pattern is greatly dependent on modulation frequency value. For a modulation amplitude comparable with the steady one the laser diode dynamics exhibits bifurcation of period doubling that can result in chaotic behavior.

articleTitle: Geometric phase applications to ISAR image compression
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The work introduces a method for ISAR image compression based on the geometric phase decomposition. Complex 2D radar data can be compressed in cross-range (Doppler frequency) dimension several times without significant image smearing and without loss of phase information. With the help of joint time-frequency analysis, target motion can still be recovered from the compressed image. For a stepped-frequency ISAR an image with a given compression ratio can be obtained directly as a portion of radar time-history series without any additional processing.

articleTitle: Space leakage of power from uniplanar transmission lines
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Surface and space leakage of power deteriorates the operation of circuits. On the other hand space leaky waves enable the design of specific radiators. We therefore investigate the potential of the slotline and the coplanar waveguide to radiate into space. We confirm the findings of earlier studies and extend them to higher order modes as regards the slotline, and report analogous new findings on the coplanar waveguide.

articleTitle: MOCVD grown AlInAs/GaInAs/InP HEMTs with InP etch-stop layer
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: We report on MOCVD grown single delta doped AlInAs/GaInAs/InP HEMTs. The devices' small-signal behavior at room and cryogenic temperatures were evaluated. It is found that HEMTs with a thin InP top surface layer provide high threshold voltage uniformity, and less thermal stress degradation compared to conventional AlInAs/GaInAs/InP HEMTs. Furthermore, hot electron stress measurements have been conducted on passivated and unpassivated HEMTs.

articleTitle: Optical and electrical low-frequency noise and their correlation measurements in InGaAsP MQW lasers
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: In this study, the experimental investigation results of InGaAsP multi-quantum-well (MQW) ridge-waveguide Fabry-Perot lasers are presented. Comprehensive studies of the optical and electrical low-frequency noise spectral densities have been carried out under wide laser current and temperature range. At defined currents and/or temperatures, the very strongly correlated electrical and optical noise with Lorentzian type spectrum were observed in Fabry-Perot diode operation due to the mode intensity hopping effect.

articleTitle: FDTD simulation of the soliton propagation in the optical fiber
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: This paper presents a procedure based on the finite difference time domain (FDTD) method, for efficiently solving the nonlinear Schrodinger equation, which has a stable solution called soliton. The numerical routines were implemented in the program for numerically solving a nonlinear Schrodinger equation, written using the computer software MATLAB, which enables observation of solitons, includes losses and third-order dispersion and gives a graphical representation of soliton propagation in two and three dimensions.

articleTitle: Researching of multidimensional coordinates estimation of an object in a radar with two dimensional electronic scanning with using real echo-signals
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The results of multidimensional coordinate estimation of two fixed point objects by a radar with two-dimensional electronically controlled pencil beam are shown. Detection is realised in MTD structure and then range, azimuth, elevation, Doppler frequency and their statistics are determined. In this way the coordinate estimation algorithms are verified in real conditions.

articleTitle: Advanced design of re-entrant beam distributed-emission crossed-field tubes
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The computed and measured results for re-entrant beam, distributed emission, crossed-field tubes are presented. The computer modelling is carried out by a particle-in-cell method (PIC method) in quasi-periodic, single-mode and non-relativistic approximations. The PIC method provides an accurate means to accomplish the computer modelling of classical continuous-wave magnetron generators including the low-voltage magnetron as well as the millimeter wave magnetron. The 3D self-consistent mathematical model of the non-traditional magnetron generator (combined magnetron) is considered.

articleTitle: Transmitter position estimation methods demonstrated on a GPS-SDMA-system
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Different methods to estimate the position of transmitters in a SDMA system are presented. To achieve the required position detection accuracy in a SDMA system the parameter estimation of the transmitter positions is performed by classical methods (based on the Fourier transform) as well as parametrical high-resolution methods (eigenanalysis-based methods and autoregressive methods). The position detection accuracy of these methods is compared using a two-transmitter constellation for a GPS satellite tracking system with a smart antenna.

articleTitle: KLL-sphere as tool for problem solving in radar remote sensing
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Approximate permittivity characteristics of media can be connected to relative measurements with coherent polarimetric radar. On the basis of theoretical considerations, attention is paid to experimental verification and imaging on the so-called KLL-sphere.

articleTitle: Determination of dielectric permittivity at microwaves using the eigenvalue problem
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A simple method for solving the inverse medium problem to determine the complex dielectric permittivity of a dielectric material at microwave frequencies is presented. The arbitrarily shaped dielectric sample is considered to be placed in a rectangular waveguide. The finite-difference technique and harmonic functions are applied to get a system of linear equations with measured reflection and/or transition coefficients added and solved through the eigenvalue problem. An algorithm to distinguish proper results from the system eigenvalues is defined by considering numerical solution properties. The system is tested using another method.

articleTitle: Synthesis and analysis of system of Walsh-Cooley basis functions
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The method of Walsh system formation which provides linearization of frequency scales at the input and the output of the discrete Fourier transform is considered, the design of a fast implementation of which coincides with the Cooley-Tukey algorithm.

articleTitle: Fuzzy algorithm for multidimensional clustering and elementary detections estimation
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: As the result of using a pencil beam in 3D radar, elementary detections, which come from one target, occur in few adjacent positions of the antenna beam. Similar operation is called data fuzzyfication in fuzzy logic. For the purpose of obtaining the best quality coefficient of single and group target discrimination it is necessary to use a clustering of elementary detection algorithm and parameter estimation based on elementary detection of the discriminating group. The modified fuzzy c-mean algorithm presented allows both multidimensional discrimination and estimation of the m-parameter target group.

articleTitle: Ka-band autooscillating instrumentation for resonator Q-measurement by phase method
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Instrumentation for high quality-factor measurement of Ka-band resonators by phase method is described. An autooscillating scheme with automatic frequency control system is used in the set-up. This scheme transfers amplification on an intermediate frequency. Examples of measurement of quality factors and estimates of measurement error are given for the open mirror and quasioptical dielectric resonators. The instrumentation is cheaper than frequency-synthesizer-based Q-meters.

articleTitle: Planar array antenna for secondary radar synthesis
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The article offers a solution for a planar aperture amplitude and phase distribution of an antenna for secondary radar or monopulse radar utilization. Primary requests for design are low sidelobes and optimum coverage in both horizontal and vertical planes in the main channel (suma) and also sufficient receiver sidelobes suppression in channel delta.

articleTitle: The use of the equivalence principle "on the average" for modeling a random complex radar object based on the fine structure of the polarization-angular response function
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The paper demonstrates application of the equivalence principle "on the average" which is evaluated to model random complex radar objects. The model makes use of the fine structure of the scattering polarization-angular response function.

articleTitle: Energy measurement error caused by finite directivity of the reflectometer
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The importance of accurate energy measurement during a microwave heating process as well as operation of a simplified measurement system for scientific research of the heating process are briefly recalled in the paper. A detailed description of the error components caused by the finite directivity of the couplers creating a reflectometer is given. A dependence of energy measurement error on the finite directivity as a function of reflection coefficient is different from such dependence when reflection coefficient only is measured.

articleTitle: Radar reflection from surfaces with ruptures
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: In some radar earth observation problems, it is necessary to investigate reflections from structures with internal ruptures such as fractures in ice ravines or all kinds of hollow spaces. Polarimetric radar may sense the structure of ruptures by doing measurements under different observation angles. Experimental data show that the reflection coefficient may have a significant magnitude. Pit walls which deviate from fully parallel walls can also cause this effect. Analysis based on models therefore must always be extended very carefully. In this paper, models for structures with internal ruptures in the form of a wedge-shaped fracture are proposed. In general, the radar senses the structure with a rupture under a specific angle using an antenna with a given antenna pattern. Relationships between the reflection coefficient at observation angle /spl theta/, the geometrical dimensions and the electrophysical parameters of the pit must then be determined. Strictly speaking, diffraction theory is needed to solve such problems. However, if we assume that the dimensions of the pit are much larger than the wavelength, geometrical-optics approximations turn out to be very fruitful. Numerical results are shown.

articleTitle: New properties of wave behavior within periodic ferrite media
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: New properties of wave behavior within layered ferrite media are presented. Conditions of propagation of periodic waves with period that is equal to n periods of structure are presented. For investigation the translation matrix method is used.

articleTitle: Scattering in a section of rectangular waveguide with a pseudochiral /spl Omega/ slab
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The mode matching approach is applied to a rectangular waveguide containing a pseudochiral /spl Omega/ slab. From waveguide measurements carried out over a few placements of the slab in the guide the constitutive parameters are extracted. The extraction is performed numerically by a algorithm minimizing the difference between theoretical and measured values of resonance frequency and scattering parameters. The field displacement phenomenon becomes visible by the frequency responses of the scattering parameters and E-field patterns. The measured and theoretical results show the resonance effects which may be applicable in design of bandstop filters.

articleTitle: 6-bit digital frequency discriminator for the 6-18 GHz band
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The concept and structure of a 6-bit frequency discriminator are presented and measurement results are given. Also problems encountered during the realization of the discriminator are discussed.

articleTitle: A more accurate determining the noise figure of microwave amplifiers
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A more precise method for determining the frequency dependency of noise figures for microwave amplifiers is briefly presented. The method can be used effectively by SPICE and C.I.A. (circuit interactive analyzer) programs. In comparison with the primary method using the SPICE program, graphic results can also be obtained during the run of the C.I.A. program without the necessity of numerical postprocessing. Moreover, the frequency dependency of the noise figure may also be optimized to achieve better results from a technical point of view. Graphic results of an example are also presented.

articleTitle: On the left eigenvectors of Stroh matrices
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The Stroh formalism is becoming a popular tool in the analysis of surface waves and related phenomena in anisotropic solids and piezoelectrics. It is shown that the left eigenvectors of a nonsymmetric matrix resulting from the Stroh system of equations governing wave motion in anisotropic piezoelectric halfspace, as well as of the analogous Stroh matrix for the electromagnetic case of certain anisotropic media, can be obtained by simple manipulation of its right eigenvectors. This can be helpful in many calculations exploiting the Stroh formalism, for example in evaluation of a functional approximation to the planar harmonic Green's function of anisotropic media.

articleTitle: Bit error probability of QPSK system in the presence of noise and multiple sine interferences
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to determine the error probability in detecting a QPSK signal. The phase-locked loop (PLL) of first order is used in providing the synchronization reference signal extraction, which is assumed to be imperfect. The bit error probability is determined when the signal interference and Gaussian noise are applied to the input of the QPSK receiver. The interference is approximated by a sum of sine waves with constant amplitudes and uniformly distributed phases.

articleTitle: Wideband receiving module of 1.5 MMW range based on metal dielectric waveguide
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The article describes the receiving module and reviews investigation results in the band of 183-207 GHz. The module is capable of simultaneous reception at 183.310 GHz (H/sub 2/O), 184.378 GHz, 206.132 GHz (ozone), 204.352 GHz (ClO) and can be employed in spectrometers and radio measuring devices for the EHF range.

articleTitle: Dynamics of spin wave solitons in the region of small wave numbers
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The results of numerical simulations of nonlinear dynamics of one-dimensional pulses of backward volume magnetostatic waves are presented where the exact wave dispersion is used. The method of splitting on physical factors is utilized. It is shown that in the case of small wave numbers (k/sub 0/ /spl sim/100 cm/sup -1/), it is impossible to use any polynomial approximation for a wave dispersion; for greater wave numbers (k/sub 0/ /spl sim/400 cm/sup -1/), a parabolic approximation is suitable. We also discuss briefly the two-dimensional dynamics of nonlinear pulses.

articleTitle: A tool for microwave CAD education
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: This paper reports on a new tool which enables efficient teaching of CAD techniques where the number of students is considerable. The tool provides for automatic student training and assessment through the Internet. The tool cannot replace a teacher, however it can make the burden of repeated mechanical work less heavy, therefore providing more time for creative work.

articleTitle: Paraelectric film phase shifter
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A key component of a phased array antenna is a phase shifter. The current status of ferroelectric (and paraelectric) thin film processing enables one to expect that a tuned microwave device based on this film can be competitive with microwave ferrite and PIN diode phase shifters. An epitaxial film of BST-Ba/sub 0.5/Sr/sub 0.5/TiO/sub 3/-composition was deposited by laser ablation on an MgO substrate. With this film, a coplanar waveguide phase shifter was realized and studied. Detailed simulation of different constructions allowed the optimal design of phase shifter for MMIC to be found.

articleTitle: On the accuracy of nonlinear microwave circuit simulation at the behavioral level
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Behavioral-level simulation is a widely-used design tool for digital wireless communication systems operating at RF/microwave frequencies. However, success in using this tool depends substantially on the simulation accuracy. We consider some factors contributing to the accuracy of behavioral-level simulation. A key factor is an accurate measurement of envelope AM-AM and AM-PM transfer functions and an accurate computation of instantaneous transfer functions. Some practical recommendations how to improve the simulation accuracy are given.

articleTitle: Evaluation of dynamic range in acousto-optic phase processor
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The paper presents the results of an investigation concerning the dynamic range in an interferometric acousto-optic phase processor. Interaction between the laser light and acoustic waves results in the appearance of an interference image. There are factors which have influence on the light intensity of the interference image. Experimental results are presented for the following operating conditions of the acousto-optic phase processor-normal operating conditions, the effect of CCD camera saturation, low signals.

articleTitle: A wireless pressure-measurement system based on SAW transponder technique
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: A hybrid sensor system for tire pressure measurements is presented. We use a combination of a conventional capacitive pressure sensor together with a passive SAW transponder to build an impedance loaded reflective delay line which can be read out wirelessly. The sensor system together with a transceiver unit achieved a pressure resolution of at least /spl plusmn/ 0.15 kPa within a measurement range of 100 to 400 kPa.

articleTitle: Highly effective asymmetric reflector antennas of Cassegrain type
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Each antenna presents a considerable contribution to the energy balance of a radio link. It performs two tasks: amplification of a received/transmitted signal and practical performance of space selection of radiation direction. Quantitative parameters describing these tasks are energy gain and radiation pattern (mainlobe width and sidelobe level), respectively. Growing demands concerning radioelectronic systems imply more severe requirements for antennas applied there. The search for a new solution in reflecting antenna design is still a problem to be solved. Reflecting antennas are in some cases hardly replaceable in spite of many existing satisfactory multibeam array structures. At present double reflecting antennas are mostly applied because of some advantages over single-reflecting ones. The most important is their possibility of considerably greater directivity value due to greater uniformity of radiated field distribution. We show a comparison between field distribution in apertures of both single and double reflector antennas. In both cases a uniform source radiation pattern is assumed. An additional and essential advantage of a double-reflector antenna is a very convenient location of the radiating source supply feeder, at the rear part of the reflector.

articleTitle: Novel, multilayer coupled-line structures and their circuit applications
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Presented are characteristics of new (or described in the literature but not in detail) symmetric and asymmetric coupled-line structures which are of use in the design of quasi-ideal multilayer microstrip and coplanar directional couplers as well as other coupled-line passive components for monolithic and hybrid microwave integrated circuits. In several designs of tightly and weakly coupled multistrip lines, the coupling coefficient can be achieved in a large range of values, enabling at the same time their quasi-ideal realisation for a given dielectric stratification of the structure. This property allows the design of high-performance multisection coupled-line passive circuits, which are very sensitive to how much the coupling coefficients for individual coupled-line sections differ from the values determined by the circuit synthesis methods. The investigated structures have been used in the design and practical realisation of the following integrated circuits: single- and multi-section coupled-line directional couplers, filters, phase shifters and power dividers, as well as coupled-line compensated baluns, non-reflective multiple pin-diode attenuators/DPDT switches, compact multidimensional Butler matrices, and broadband in-phase antenna array feeding networks. We include the design data and experimental results for most of the circuits we describe. The paper presents the results of the authors' research into the properties and applications of new microstrip and coplanar lines from the period of the past few years. Some of the most recent results (not yet published) are also presented.

articleTitle: Ultra-low-noise, InP field effect transistor radio astronomy receivers: state-of-the-art
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Recent developments in ultra-low-noise, cryogenically-cooled, heterostructure field-effect transistor (HFET) receivers for frequencies up to 118 GHz are reviewed. Design and examples of the realization of InP HFET amplifiers and receivers in the frequency range 3 to 118 GHz are described. Applications to ultra-low-noise radioastronomy receivers, as well as broadband continuum radiometers, are discussed.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic modelling for microwave heating applications
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Microwave power applications are nowadays wide-spread throughout industry, science, and private households. The best known is thermal processing of foods, but one should also note drying of textiles, fibres, paper and board, preheating and curing of plastics and rubber, and controlling chemical reactions. In all these areas, a majority of design work on microwave heating systems and processes has been based on intuitive perceptions and engineering experience. Electromagnetic modelling, which is a potentially powerful alternative, is rarely considered and almost never used. The idea behind this paper is to enhance the use of electromagnetic modelling in microwave power industry and research. Modelling may provide a new level of knowledge on what simplifications can or cannot be made, and be an important tool for analysing causes of unacceptable variability in production.

articleTitle: Very high efficiency microwave amplifier. The harmonic manipulation approach
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The harmonic manipulation approach represents the best solution to improve power amplifier performance. Remarkable improvements in terms of output power, power gain and power added efficiency is demonstrated, suggesting different solutions, which represent a trade off between achievable performances and circuit complexity. While explaining some of the contradictory results already reported in the literature and giving a physical insight to the harmonic manipulation mechanism, the proposed approach suggests some useful guidelines for the microwave amplifier design. Finally, experimental results obtained at 5 GHz and 20 GHz confirm the feasibility of the proposed approach, both in the microwave and millimetre wave range.

articleTitle: Microwave remote sensing of dangerous meteorological phenomena
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Techniques of microwave remote sensing of the atmosphere with the emphasis on aviation applications are considered. Some results obtained during the last few years are presented.

articleTitle: Smart antennas for mobile communications systems
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The paper presents an outline of the most important problems related to the development of advanced base station antennas which are referred to as smart antennas. They are needed by new generations of mobile communications systems. Smart antennas involve not only RF components but also a broad segment of digital beamforming and digital signal processing units.

articleTitle: Recent advances in polarimetric-interferometric SAR theory and technology and its application
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The development of radar polarimetry and radar interferometry is advancing rapidly. Whereas with radar polarimetry the textural fine-structure, target orientation, symmetries and material constituents can be recovered with considerable improvement above that of standard "amplitude-only" radar, with radar interferometry the spatial (in depth) structure can be explored. In "polarimetric interferometric synthetic aperture radar (POL-IN-SAR) imaging", it is possible to recover such co-registered textural and spatial information from POL-IN-SAR digital image data sets simultaneously, including the extraction of digital elevation maps (DEM) from either polarimetric (scattering matrix) or interferometric (single platform: dual antenna) SAR systems. Simultaneous polarimetric-plus-interferometric SAR offers the additional benefit of obtaining co-registered textural-plus-spatial three-dimensional POL-IN-DEM information, which, when applied to repeat-pass image-overlay interferometry, provides differential background validation, stress assessment and environmental stress-change information with high accuracy. Then, either designing "multiple dual-polarization antenna POL-IN-SAR" systems or applying advanced "POL-IN-SAR image compression techniques" will result in "POLarimetric TOMOgraphic (multi-interferometric) SAR" or "POL-TOMO-SAR" imaging. This is of direct relevance to wide-area, dynamic battle-space surveillance and local-to-global environmental background validation, stress assessment and stress-change monitoring of terrestrial and planetary surface covers.

articleTitle: Influence of advanced GaAs MMICs on structure and cost of high frequency communication and radar systems for volume markets
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Following the rapid expansion of mobile communication systems the access and overlay networks are extensively employing GaAs MMIC in order to improve producibility for the required production quantities and to enable the first phase of cost reduction. A new generation of MMIC is now emerging which is based on multifunctional integration. This approach could reduce the number of MMIC presently used by more than 50% with a respective influence on the cost of the high-frequency frontends. This could be a key step towards the introduction of broadband wireless access to the home for really consumer-oriented markets (wireless Internet to the home, LMDS, MVDS).

articleTitle: Advances in computational dosimetry
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: Numerical dosimetry is becoming an increasingly important tool in the evaluations of exposures to electromagnetic fields from extremely low frequencies to millimeter waves. To be effective a numerical dosimetry system has to comprise three key elements: an accurate computer model of the human body, a robust numerical technique and appropriate testing protocols. Recent progress in these areas is reported.

articleTitle: The application of network methods to distributed microwave circuit analysis
publicationTitle: 13th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications. MIKON - 2000. Conference Proceedings (IEEE Cat. No.00EX428)
abstract: The application of network methods to electromagnetic field problems is discussed. The field problem is systematically treated by the segmentation technique and by specifying canonical Foster representations for the subcircuits. Connection between different subdomains is obtained by selecting the appropriate independent field quantities via Tellegen's theorem. For each subdomain, as well as for the entire circuit, an equivalent circuit extraction procedure is feasible, either in closed form for subdomains amenable to analytical description or via the relevant pole structure description when a numerical solution is available. Several numerical examples are provided, based on modal techniques as well as on transmission line matrix (TLM) modeling.
